# Hands on with AI Observability

Welcome to this hands-on, interactive lab. The lab is structured into exercises. Estimated completion times are provided.

All exercises are self-contained. You can complete all exercises or pick and choose the ones that interest you.

## Estimated Completion Times

| Number | Exercise    | Completion Time (mins) |
| ---    | ---         | ---                    |
| 1      | Model Calling with Guardrails | 2  |
| 2      | AI Safety: Guardrails | 2     |
| 3      | Agentic Tool Calling | 3 |

## Exercise 1: Model Calling with Guardrails

### Search for a destination

Go to `http://localhost:8080` and search for `Sydney`.

After about 30s (it's slow since the AI model is running locally on this laptop), a result will be returned.

![Distributed Trace](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/app-ui-sydney.png?raw=true)

### View traces

[Open the distributed tracing app (right click and open in new window)](/ui/apps/dynatrace.distributedtracing/explorer?filter=dt.entity.service.entity.name+%3D+ai-travel-advisor)

A distributed trace is the end-to-end flow of work, visualised in a way that is easily digestible. Each operation taken by the application creates a distributed trace.


![Distributed Trace](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/distributed-trace-2.png?raw=true)

## Trace Explained

Each node in this trace shows a step in the process of retrieving the travel destination advice.

Overall the task took `10.42 seconds`. Time runs left to right. Tasks and subtasks are nested below one another (these are called `spans` and `sub spans`).

1. A guardrail was evaluated and passed successfully (there are no errors / warnings shown)
1. Ollama (the AI model provider) was called for an answer

Highlighting each node (span) shows you important metadata attached to each step. Expand the `guard` node and keep expanding until you see the `is-travel-related.validate` span. Highlight this span.

![AI guardrail](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/ai-guardrail-2.png?raw=true)

This guardrail evaluation took `86 milliseconds`. It's clear to see that when presented with an input of `Sydney` the guardrail decision was `pass` and thus the model was called.

Now highlight the `ollama.chat` span. The important metadata is available:

- How long did it take the model to response? (Answer: `10.05 seconds`)
- What model was used to retrieve this response? (Answer: `qwen3:0.6b`)
- What prompt was the model given? (Answer: `# Role: City expert. # Task: Provide three positive things to do for the given city.`)
- What response did the model give back? (Answer: `- **Visit Sydney Park** – Explore the city’s green spaces, including iconic gardens and walking trails for a peaceful retreat...`)
- How many tokens were consumed for this request? (Answer: `66` input tokens and `324` output tokens.)

![Ollama Response](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/ollama-response-2.png?raw=true)

## Exercise 2: AI Safety (Guardrails)

Our application should only be used to generate travel advice. Any other use should be prevented. Our guardrail should prevent that.

Try searching for this phrase: `Which stocks should I invest in for 2026?`

![AI guardrail](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/app-ui-ai-guardrail-blocked-2.png?raw=true)

Refresh [the distributed tracing app](/ui/apps/dynatrace.distributedtracing/explorer?filter=dt.entity.service.entity.name+%3D+ai-travel-advisor) and notice a second trace (which executes much more quickly).

![Failed Trace](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/failed-trace-2.png?raw=true)

Again, expand the `guard` node and highlight the `is-travel-related.validate` span. Notice that is has taken an input of `Which stocks should I invest in for 2026?` and thrown an exception + error message.

Importantly also note that Ollama is *not* called (we safely blocked abuse of the LLM using this guardrail).

![AI guardrail fail](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/guardrail-failed-banned-topic.png?raw=true)

## Exercise 3: Agentic Tool Calling

![AI agent + tool architecture](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/agentic-tools-architecture.jpg?raw=true)

AI Agents are autonomous processes that act in a so called [ReAct loop](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/react-agent) until a goal they're provided is met.

Agents can be provided with "tools" which can be thought of as "capabilities".

In this exercise, we provide an agent with a goal.

### Goal

Given a current location and a destination, answer three questions:
1) What's the weather like at the destination?
2) How far away is the current location from the destination?
3) What is the flight time from the current location to the destination?

### Tools

The agent is also provided 3 tools:

- Ability to look up the location (latitude and longitude) of a given city
- Ability to calculate the distance between two places
- Ability to get the weather of a given city

### Start the Agent

Switch to VS Code and open the `exercise 3` terminal window.

Run this command:

```
python tool.calling.py --destination "San Francisco"
```

As it runs you should see output as the agent decides to retrieve the geo-locations for the current location (`Las Vegas` of course) and the destination (`San Francisco`).

At the end of the run you'll see lots of raw output and a hyperlink to the distributed traces screen in Dynatrace. Ctrl + Click that hyperlink and highlight the trace.

![agentic trace](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/agentic-trace.png?raw=true)

You should see a number of `tools.task` spans and at least one call to Ollama (a `model.task` span).

Just like before, expand each span and navigate around the metadata until you understand how the agent worked in that particular. It usually decides to look up a few locations, and the weather then call Ollama with the information.

Notice that each usage of the `get_location_coordinates` tool does a `GET` request to the OpenStreetMap API which is also traced.

### View the result

![agentic result metadata](https://github.com/agardnerIT/OddFiles/blob/master/p26/agentic-result.png?raw=true)

Highlight the final `ChatOllama.chat` node and notice the `gen ai` metadata. You should be able to see:

- The input prompt: `Answer three questions: 1) What's the weather like in San Francisco? 2) How far away from Las Vegas is San Francisco? 3) What is the flight time from Las Vegas to San Francisco?`
- The output result: `1) The weather in San Francisco is overcast with a current temperature of 8.6°C. 2) San Francisco is approximately 573.87 kilometers away from Las Vegas, taking about 1.15 hours to fly. 3) The flight time from Las Vegas to San Francisco is approximately 1.15 hours.`
- The system prompt: `You are a helpful assistant that can check the weather and tell me how far places are from each other. If a tool exists for a task, you must use it. Call tools more than once when required. Prefer a tool than calling the model.`
- Token counts

## 🎉Lab Finished

Congratulations, you have completed the AI Observability hands on lab.

Obviously we only convered a tiny portion of what's possible. We didn't even have time to look at logs or metrics, but hopefully this gives a sense of what's possible.

If you would like the code behind these demo please speak to booth staff who will send it through after Perform 2026.

If you have any comments or suggestions please reach out to `devrel@dynatrace.com`
